lake-build-guard.sh replayed a GREEN result that never covered an edited file. Sequence: the Phase 2 full build ran 11:35:52-12:04:03 and compiled PlusReversal.lean at 11:36:56; a docstring-only edit to that same file landed at 11:41:15, mid-build; the guard's post_fingerprint is taken at build END (12:04:03) and therefore captured the ALREADY-EDITED tree. A subsequent identical invocation then satisfied all three replay conditions (state=complete, matching scope_key, 'unchanged' tree) and emitted 'REPLAY: sharing result from holder pid 2379146, age 332s, recorded exit status 0' without running lake at all. The replayed log is byte-identical to the first, including per-target timings, so the only tells are the REPLAY: line on stderr and the .olean mtime (11:36:56) still predating the source (11:41:15). Two lessons: never edit a source file while a guarded build is in flight, and verify a build with the .olean-newer-than-source check rather than trusting guard exit 0 plus a success line. Resolved by re-running with --no-share, which the guard documents as 'Never replay a prior result; always run a real build'.
